sequential_dependency.intermediate: The canonically completed grid together with the newly completed target coordinates grouped by color, their per-color completion counts, and the unique color with the greatest completion count.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Inspect every 2x2 window in the original input, identify each three-equal-nonzero plus one-zero completion target, and apply all such fills simultaneously.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Using that intermediate, connect only the winning color between pairs of its newly completed targets that share a row or column, painting through still-zero cells.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: B needs A to produce both its route endpoints and the completion-count winner. A raw-input color-frequency substitute selects the large solid runner-up color instead, so the protected-Racket counterfactual routes the wrong target set and changes the final grid.

parametric_work.summary: Two settings are source-inventoried and native-qualified on seeds 0 and 17 with two visible demonstrations and four queries. The default is byte-exact canonical; the alternative performs canonical completion, derives a completion-count winner, then routes aligned new targets. Finite self-audit found no demo-surviving rival that changed a query.
